title: What is Flexbox?
overview: Flexbox is a layout system used in React Native to arrange components inside a container. It helps create flexible and responsive layouts by controlling the size, direction, and alignment of elements.

title: Understanding flex Property
overview: The flex property defines how much available space a component should take inside its parent container. It allows components to grow and adjust according to screen size.

title: flexDirection
overview: flexDirection determines the direction in which child components are arranged. React Native uses column as the default direction, placing items vertically.

title: justifyContent
overview: justifyContent controls the alignment of children along the main axis. It is used to distribute space and position components inside a container.

title: alignItems
overview: alignItems controls the alignment of children along the opposite axis. It is commonly used to center or position components horizontally.

title: flexWrap and Multiple Rows
overview: flexWrap allows child components to move into a new row or column when there is not enough available space. It is useful for layouts containing multiple items.

title: Gap, Margin and Padding with Flexbox
overview: Spacing properties like gap, margin, and padding help create proper distance between components while using Flexbox layouts.

example.title: Spacing Example

title: Creating Responsive Layouts Using Flexbox
overview: Flexbox helps create layouts that work across different screen sizes and devices. Using flex values, alignment properties, and flexible dimensions makes applications responsive.
